name: Produced water treatment (hydrocyclones, flotation, membranes)
principle: Water produced with oil is treated by gravity separators, hydrocyclones, plate coalescers, dissolved gas flotation and nutshell filters before discharge or reinjection. Radioactive radium in some brines (above 3,500 pCi/L in one sample) adds disposal constraints; membranes are not covered by the page read.

process_steps.name: Polishing filters, then discharge or reinjection

performance.metric: radium in an Ohio brine sample
performance.basis: NRC discharge limit below 60 pCi/L for Ra-226 and Ra-228

source.note: Wikipedia, Produced water, read 25 October 2026 (secondary source)

performance.metric: OSPAR dispersed-oil-in-produced-water discharge performance standard (NE Atlantic offshore)
performance.unit: mg oil per litre discharged (average annual performance standard)
performance.basis: OSPAR offshore discharges report tables list "installations for which the average annual oil content of the produced water discharged to the sea exceeds the 30 mg/l performance standard"; treatment to below the standard is by hydrocyclones/flotation, for which the sources read state no single efficiency figure

source.note: OSPAR Commission, Offshore Industry Series: report on discharges, spills and emissions from offshore oil and gas installations (read 2026-10-28)

limitations: The page gives no discharge limits in mg/L or membrane performance
